articles.title: Iran Commander Warns US After Fresh Tensions; Says Every 'Iranian Death Will Be Answered In Kind'
articles.description: Iran has issued another strong warning to the United States as regional tensions continue to simmer. Major General Ali Abdollahi, commander of Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, said that every Iranian killed would be answered by the death of an American soldier, according to Iranian state-affiliated media. He described the policy as a standing military principle and claimed it had already been demonstrated in previous confrontations. The remarks come amid months of military exchanges, heightened activity across the Gulf and repeated Iranian claims of strikes on US military facilities.

articles.title: Bill introduced in US Senate seeks 3-year pause on H-1B visas, codify $100,000 fee
articles.description: A US Republican senator has introduced a bill seeking to pause new H-1B visa issuances for three years and restore a $100,000 fee on H-1B petitions introduced by the Trump administration but struck down by a court. The proposed End H-1B Abuse Act aims to tighten eligibility rules, replace the visa lottery with a wage-based system, restrict outsourcing models, and curb benefits for visa holders' dependents.

articles.title: No specific law authorises live facial recognition at protests, legal experts warn
articles.description: India currently lacks specific laws authorizing police facial recognition use at public gatherings. Lawyers warn that such deployments may face constitutional challenges and privacy concerns. The Supreme Court's privacy ruling requires strict safeguards for any technology use. A comprehensive parliamentary framework is needed to regulate facial recognition technology. Non-matching facial data should be deleted immediately after searches.

articles.title: Psychology says people who ask others to move a little bit and let them sit even if there is not much space in metro, train, bus or other public transport aren't being inconsiderate: What this behavior may reveal?
articles.description: Psychology says people who ask others to move a bit and let them sit even if there is not much space in public transport aren't always trying to inconvenience others.
